scenes.tts: If damage to a structure wipes out a memory, was the memory stored there?
scenes.visual: Title fades. A brain region is erased and a memory icon vanishes. A question mark: stored there?
scenes.narration: If damage to a structure wipes out a memory, was the memory stored there?

scenes.tts: In rabbits, a tone is paired with a puff of air to the eye.
scenes.visual: A rabbit schematic. A speaker gives a tone; a nozzle sends a puff to the eye. A timeline: tone bar, then puff mark overlapping its end.
scenes.narration: In rabbits, a tone is paired with a puff of air to the eye.

scenes.tts: After training, the tone alone closes the eyelid before the puff. The puff itself always triggers a reflex blink.
scenes.visual: An eyelid trace: a closure begins before the puff mark, labelled conditioned response; a sharper closure right after the puff, labelled reflex blink.
scenes.narration: After training, the tone alone closes the eyelid before the puff. The puff itself always triggers a reflex blink.

scenes.tts: In 1982, Thompson's laboratory removed the lateral cerebellum on the same side as the trained eye.
scenes.visual: A rabbit brain from above; the lateral cerebellum on the trained eye's side is shaded and removed. Label: 1982.
scenes.narration: In 1982, Thompson's laboratory removed the lateral cerebellum on the same side as the trained eye.

scenes.tts: The learned response to the tone was abolished.
scenes.visual: The eyelid trace: the closure before the puff is gone.
scenes.narration: The learned response to the tone was abolished.

scenes.tts: Was the eyelid simply paralysed? If so, what would happen to the reflex blink to the puff?
scenes.visual: The reflex part of the trace is greyed out with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Was the eyelid simply paralysed? If so, what would happen to the reflex blink to the puff?

scenes.tts: It would fail too. But the reflex blink survived, so the eyelid could still move.
scenes.visual: The reflex closure returns in full after the puff. Tick: can still move.
scenes.narration: It would fail too. But the reflex blink survived, so the eyelid could still move.

scenes.tts: And the other eye could still be conditioned. So the rabbits could still hear the tone, and still learn.
scenes.visual: The other eye's trace develops a closure before the puff. Ticks: can hear, can learn.
scenes.narration: And the other eye could still be conditioned. So the rabbits could still hear the tone, and still learn.

scenes.tts: With these controls, the lost response is good evidence that the cerebellum is needed for it.
scenes.visual: Card: single dissociation plus controls. Ruled out: paralysis, deafness, a general loss of learning. A tick beside needed.
scenes.narration: With these controls, the lost response is good evidence that the cerebellum is needed for it.

scenes.tts: But needed for what? A lost response cannot tell a lost store from a cut output route.
scenes.visual: A circuit: tone in, a box labelled store?, a cable to the eyelid. Two versions side by side: box erased; cable cut. Both give the same flat trace.
scenes.narration: But needed for what? A lost response cannot tell a lost store from a cut output route.

scenes.tts: A later experiment silenced the output route with a drug, only during training. No learned response appeared. Once the drug wore off, it was there. The rabbits had learned.
scenes.visual: The same circuit. The cable to the eyelid dims, labelled silenced during training; the trace stays flat. The cable lights again and the closure before the puff appears at once. Label: needed to express, not where it was learned.
scenes.narration: A later experiment silenced the output route with a drug, only during training. No learned response appeared. Once the drug wore off, it was there. The rabbits had learned.

scenes.tts: H M's brain raises a second limit: which structure was needed? After his death in 2008, it was cut into thousands of thin sections and rebuilt in three dimensions.
scenes.caption: H.M.'s brain raises a second limit: which structure was needed? After his death in 2008, it was cut into thousands of thin sections and rebuilt in three dimensions.
scenes.visual: A schematic human brain with the medial temporal lobes outlined. Thin slices stack into a 3D model of the brain. Labels: 2008; 2,401 block-face images.
scenes.narration: H.M.'s brain raises a second limit: which structure was needed? After his death in 2008, it was cut into thousands of thin sections and rebuilt in three dimensions.

scenes.tts: The operation had taken the front of the hippocampus, most of the amygdala, and nearly all the entorhinal cortex.
scenes.visual: In the 3D model, the anterior hippocampus, most of the amygdala and nearly all the entorhinal cortex are shown as missing, each labelled.
scenes.narration: The operation had taken the front of the hippocampus, most of the amygdala, and nearly all the entorhinal cortex.

scenes.tts: But the back of the hippocampus remained on both sides, with neurons still present.
scenes.visual: The posterior hippocampus glows on both sides. Label: about 2 cm³ each side; neurons in CA1 to CA4. A card: both hippocampi removed, struck through.
scenes.narration: But the back of the hippocampus remained on both sides, with neurons still present.

scenes.tts: The entorhinal cortex is the main cortical route into the hippocampus. What remained may have been largely cut off.
scenes.visual: The entorhinal cortex drawn as a cable into the hippocampus; the cable is cut where the entorhinal cortex is missing.
scenes.narration: The entorhinal cortex is the main cortical route into the hippocampus. What remained may have been largely cut off.

scenes.tts: The authors offered that as a model. Living cells in a section do not prove they were connected or working.
scenes.visual: A label over the cut cable: a model, not a measurement. A stained section with cell bodies and a question mark: working?
scenes.narration: The authors offered that as a model. Living cells in a section do not prove they were connected or working.

scenes.tts: So his amnesia followed a medial temporal lesion on both sides. His case alone cannot assign it to one structure.
scenes.visual: The whole lesion outlined as one region. Arrows to the hippocampus, amygdala and entorhinal cortex each carry a question mark.
scenes.narration: So his amnesia followed a medial temporal lesion on both sides. His case alone cannot assign it to one structure.

scenes.tts: Crossed failures show that the damaged tissue is needed for a task. They do not tell you where memories live.
scenes.visual: End card: Lesions show what is needed, not where memories live.
scenes.narration: Crossed failures show that the damaged tissue is needed for a task. They do not tell you where memories live.
